title: Brainstorm: Amazon as a personal attic service
why: Speculative product wish with no technical or factual substance; mostly a joke-like idea about renting out storage.

title: Anecdote about buying an espresso machine
why: Personal gift story with no transferable lesson about espresso or pizza; the buying advice is never delivered.

title: Argument that all work is necessary
why: Opinionated economic argument built on rough assumptions; it makes a claim rather than teaching a verifiable mechanism.

title: Using Gmail Inbox as a to-do system
why: Pinning marks actionable mail and snoozing defers it; clusters at fixed times keep the inbox working like a task list.

title: Opinion on Reddit's golang subreddit deletion
why: Reactive opinion about a platform controversy; the technical remark about editing raw data is not developed into a lesson.

title: Indie publisher on Internet Archive lawsuit
why: Advocacy for publishers' rights in a lawsuit; a position statement rather than an explanation a reader would learn from.

title: Launch order to protect an app's name
why: Register the domain, then ship iOS, then Android, then web; a web-first launch let a copycat claim the Android listing.

title: Argument against a natural right to anonymity
why: Political-philosophy argument framed as a challenge to opponents; it argues a position rather than explaining a fact or mechanism.

title: Defense of leased ISP routers for consumers
why: Opinion on support tradeoffs and personal time value; it argues a cost-benefit view without new technical or factual insight.

title: Speculation on why hopeful content gets fewer views
why: Unsupported guess about audience preferences, offered as opinion with no evidence or mechanism behind it.

title: Snarky translation of Adobe's PR on HTML5
why: Commentary reading corporate PR as hostile strategy; it is witty but expresses a view rather than teaching a fact.

title: Argument that the App Store fee is rent-seeking
why: Advocacy with rough cost estimates aimed at a conclusion; the arithmetic is illustrative, not a technical explanation.

title: Why online courses beat recorded lectures
why: Polished video plus graded assignments and feedback, taken alongside peers, teach better than raw recorded lectures; assignments are the reusable asset.

title: Personal story about growing up in West Virginia
why: Biographical account of access and ambition; moving, but it teaches no transferable skill or concept.

title: Skepticism about Lightning scaling claims
why: Expresses doubt about channel topology assumptions without a worked explanation; the quoted Q&A is interesting but argumentative.

title: Complaint about architecture design tools
why: Frustration with expensive, outdated architecture software; a critique and anecdote, not a lesson about how the tools work.

title: Personal defense of 80-hour work weeks
why: Personal career philosophy and motivation; it argues a lifestyle choice rather than teaching anything technical.

title: Why 56k modems beat the Shannon limit
why: Old capacity estimates assumed an all-analog noise floor; once telephone networks went digital, the effective noise fell and the limit rose.

title: Summary of an Ars review of Windows Phone 7
why: Relays a product reviewer's opinions and quotes; useful as a record but not an explanation a reader would learn from.

title: Reply disputing claims about Stack Overflow's culture
why: Opinion about community tone and voting, argued in a debate style rather than backed by evidence or explanation.

title: Anecdote about recruiting from non-elite schools
why: A personal experience of being overlooked by recruiters; it makes a diversity argument without a transferable technical lesson.

title: Vague steep-and-decant coffee method
why: Gives an unspecified brewing outline and dares readers to argue; no ratios, temperatures or timing that would teach anything.

title: Why new CTOs struggle to stay technical
why: Fragmented days make deep technical work impossible; leaders stay useful through judgment and direction, not by taking focused tasks colleagues must maintain.

title: Engagement metrics turn media into tabloids
why: Argues that optimizing engagement erodes trust, but the claim is a broad opinion about media without evidence or a worked model.

title: Personal case for voting far-right
why: Political personal essay with contested claims; it expresses a voting rationale rather than teaching anything about the subject.

title: Why businesses resist creative software work
why: Generalized opinion about risk aversion and management; vivid, but it asserts a worldview rather than explaining a mechanism.

title: Why cloud gaming struggles with input latency
why: Streaming cannot hide latency with client-side prediction; 50ms of input lag is noticeable and home round trips plus rendering delays add up.

title: Why Lisp compiles top-level forms, not files
why: Lisp is built for REPL-style incremental compilation of tiny forms; the real hard problem is circular references across compilation units.

title: Rules-based vs principles-based regulation explained
why: Rules-based regulators are automatons; principles-based ones use discretion to resist rules-lawyering, with recourse needed when they err.

title: Summary of Assange asylum legal arguments
why: Political and legal advocacy about a high-profile case; it argues a side rather than teaching a general lesson.

title: Anecdote on AstraZeneca hesitancy in Bulgaria
why: Personal account and opinion about national policy and trust; it describes a situation rather than explaining a generalizable principle.

title: Wish for persistent browser workspaces
why: Feature request for saving tab groups as named workspaces; a user wish with no technical explanation or resource.

title: Argument that IQ tests counter hiring prejudice
why: Political argument about discrimination law framed through a story; it advocates a policy position rather than teaching a fact.

title: Why sugar makes sandwich bread soft
why: Sugar in dough gives a soft, giving crumb and lets the crust brown without hardening, which suits sandwich bread.

title: Defense of NSA staff's security motives
why: Political argument and personal anecdote about intelligence culture; it argues a stance rather than explaining a mechanism.

title: Why upstream bugs are hard to fix in practice
why: Frustration with unreviewed open-source PRs and the cost of forking; an experience-based opinion without a reusable method.

title: Most successful tech founders were 30 or older
why: A cited list of founders with ages at founding, such as Musk, Bezos and Hastings, shows most were in their 30s, not 18-22.

title: Critique of an article on AI and poverty
why: Rebuttal driven by anger at the article's framing; it argues about policy and gender rather than teaching a technique.

title: Personal account of graduating from art school
why: Reflection on a personal education choice; it offers an opinion on what art school is for, not a teachable lesson.

title: Personal account of redacted police video
why: A first-hand story about redacted footage; it illustrates distrust in policing but offers no general technical or factual lesson.

title: Skeptical take on AirPods as a platform
why: Opinion on earbuds and fashion, arguing against tech journalism; no evidence or explanation a reader would learn from.

title: Why oil is priced in dollars, debunked
why: Oil trades globally in many currencies; dollars dominate because of US consumer spending, deep markets and Fedwire speed, not a petrodollar deal.

title: How dbus was built around KDE and GNOME needs
why: Dbus was adopted by meeting the concrete requirements of KDE and GNOME developers, consolidating earlier IPC attempts instead of pursuing theoretical ideals.

title: First-hand rhabdomyolysis case from CrossFit
why: Severe delayed muscle pain after an intense first workout can signal rhabdomyolysis; creatine kinase levels can get dangerously high, so seek care early.

title: Praise for NextDNS and its ethos
why: Promotional recommendation of a DNS service with company background; a product endorsement rather than a technical explanation.

title: Defense of theaters versus streaming
why: Opinion about the big-screen experience and theater pricing; personal taste argued as a general claim.

title: Founder's account of a hosting takedown
why: One side of a hosting dispute about due process and a trademark complaint; a company grievance rather than a general lesson.

title: Opinion that social apps repeat the same cycle
why: Speculation that every broadcast app eventually adds ads and curation; a sweeping prediction without data or mechanism.

title: Question on why people and firms don't relocate
why: Asks questions about housing and migration without offering an answer or explanation; it poses rather than teaches.

title: The hidden cost of exercising startup options
why: Leaving a company means paying exercise cost plus tax on paper gains and risking total loss if the company fails; exercising early can cut the bill.

title: Argument that Facebook is not uniquely harmful
why: Opinion comparing social media to TV and MMOs; a view argued by analogy rather than shown with evidence.

title: Argument that secular philosophy lacks answers
why: Opinion on meaning and religion; it asserts a conclusion about philosophy's inferiority without a demonstrable argument or source.

title: Frustration with Netflix's homepage layout
why: A user complaint about row ordering and repeated titles; a critique of taste without a generalizable design principle.

title: Defense of cities competing for HQ2
why: Opinion about tax incentives versus infrastructure spending; the argument is economic advocacy rather than an explanation a reader would learn.

title: List of linux desktop usability complaints
why: A list of frustrations returning to Linux after years away; personal experience and complaints rather than a technique to learn.

title: Why the coffee comparison is about marginal utility
why: A dollar is trivial at the margin for most people, so app prices should be judged against spending power, not against coffee as a price benchmark.

title: Blame site bugs on single-browser testing
why: Argument that developers test only in Chrome and that this drives vendor lock-in; a sensible view but mostly opinion without data.

title: What hiring managers look for in interaction designers
why: Reject reused assets, unprototyped interactions and patchwork ideas; a strong portfolio needs usable prototypes and one coherent interaction model.

title: Doubts about a writer's HubSpot book publicity
why: Speculation about a writer's motives and PR interests; the commenter admits limited knowledge, so no lesson is taught.

title: Why Iceland's reforestation keeps failing
why: Free-range sheep eat native birch seedlings, and subsidies favor farmers over forest recovery, so planting fails unless land is fenced.

title: Requirements any error system must satisfy
why: Systems that rely on developer discipline miss errors, uniform handling fails since errors differ, and full error-type lists are infeasible.

title: Why work-sample tests beat puzzle interviews
why: Research favors judging real work samples over puzzles; they still produce false positives and negatives but predict job performance better.

title: Why ported Rust code misuses Go interfaces
why: Idiomatic Go uses small interfaces and method dispatch, not interface{} with type switches copied from Rust's pattern matching.

title: Thinking via characters instead of inner voice
why: A Chinese reader describes reasoning by recalling characters' shape and meaning, bypassing phonetic inner speech, which is faster for them.

title: Argument for Apple supporting PWAs
why: Advocacy for web apps across platforms; argues a position about fragmentation rather than explaining a technical mechanism.

title: Joke advice about unique baby names
why: Humorous suggestions about names on sanctions lists; no real explanation of how screening works beyond speculation.

title: Rant about the state of software
why: Venting about programmers ignoring support problems; frustration and anecdote, with no concrete explanation a reader would learn.

title: Argument against unpaid prison labor
why: Political argument quoting reporting on wages; it advocates a position on incarceration rather than teaching something new.

title: Personal story of learning to program on a calculator
why: A biographical account of a restricted childhood; motivating, but it teaches no transferable technical or factual lesson.

title: Skepticism that a housing boom is PR
why: Suspicion of an industry press story and its timing; an opinion about motives without data supporting the claim.

title: Argument that Wayland fragments the desktop
why: A strongly worded case against Wayland, quoting Red Hat; it argues a design critique but mostly as advocacy.

title: Defense of interstate water markets
why: Market advocacy about water rights and pipelines; an opinion piece that argues a policy view rather than explaining a mechanism.

title: Question on C++ compiler and IDE setup
why: A plea for advice about toolchains; it asks a question rather than answering one, so it teaches nothing on its own.

title: Rant about Swedish startup law burdens
why: Emotional complaint about labor and leave laws; a frustrated opinion with personal grievance rather than a teachable explanation.

title: Moderator note listing related HN threads
why: A moderator's list of linked threads and an experiment note; navigation and meta-commentary, not substantive content.

title: Deep learning is a learned input-output map
why: Practitioners struggle less with building networks than with encoding their domain as input arrays and choosing a useful output vector.

title: Moderator explanation of HN's curiosity mandate
why: A moderation note explaining why HN is not a current-affairs site; policy meta-commentary that only makes sense in context.

title: How Robinhood's order-flow payments are disclosed
why: Rule 606 reports show Robinhood receiving per-share payments from Knight and LavaFlow for routing orders, a traceable path through disclosures.

topic: fake it till you make it
title: Rant against acting like an expert
why: Moral opinion about credentials and professional honesty; it argues ethics and attitude rather than teaching a skill.

title: Why TRS-80 led the market before Apple II
why: Radio Shack's retail reach and third-party ecosystem mattered, and Apple's Disk II drive later won the market over Tandy's unreliable disk drive.

title: Forecast that low interest rates will persist
why: A macro forecast built on debt-to-income figures; plausible but a prediction and opinion rather than a settled mechanism.

title: Why dollars hold value without force
why: Dollars are accepted because they are used for taxes, pricing, reserves and insured deposits, not because the army enforces their use.

title: Why arbitration clauses bar consumer class actions
why: The Federal Arbitration Act, upheld by the Supreme Court, makes arbitration clauses and class-action waivers enforceable, constraining consumer rules.

title: Personal story on Diablo 3 auction house harm
why: A player's account of how the auction house damaged design; a game-industry opinion built on one experience.

title: Opinion against child-centered parenting
why: A critique of modern parenting norms that argues a contested values position rather than explaining evidence or a method.

title: Speculation that Facebook's decline is about video
why: Confident predictions about Facebook and TikTok trends, presented as opinion without data or analysis to support them.

title: Concern about Nvidia owning ARM
why: Opinion about Nvidia's corporate culture and the risk to the ARM ecosystem; a warning built on reputation rather than evidence.

title: Speculation on how sapiens saw Neanderthals
why: Speculative musing about perceptions of other human groups; interesting, but it offers no evidence or lesson a reader can take away.

title: Code design rules to reduce cognitive load
why: Favor declarative code, shallow call depth, separated business logic, composition over inheritance and grep-friendly names so developers can work while interrupted.

title: How cross-signing lets new CAs be trusted
why: New CAs gain trust by cross-signing with existing roots; sending the root in the chain is a misconfiguration that only slows TLS handshakes.

title: Critique of a commentator's propaganda list
why: Analysis of rhetorical tactics in a political post; it argues about how a commentary is framed rather than teaching a technical or factual point.

title: Argument for stored procedures over ORMs
why: Opinion favoring stored procedures and interfaces over ORMs; a practice preference argued from personal experience with few details.

title: How Amazon's RSU structure amplifies stock risk
why: Amazon builds a 15% share-price growth assumption into grants and caps above-band pay, so a stock drop cuts comp more than a typical refresh.

title: Programming as teaching a running program
why: Lisp and Smalltalk keep a program running while you teach it new behavior incrementally, rather than building a finished artifact from a blueprint.

title: Analysis of Twitter's valuation per user
why: Opinion that the valuation is detached from value, using per-user arithmetic; a market view argued as a warning rather than a method.

title: Argument that exposed routers are secure
why: Defends TP-Link routers using manual details and search counts; a rebuttal of a security scare that argues rather than explains.

title: Speculation that governments plan for climate collapse
why: Conspiratorial speculation linking policies to hidden climate plans; no evidence is offered, so it teaches nothing.

title: Thought experiment on brain uploads and implants
why: Speculative philosophical questions about identity and uploaded minds; provocative, but it poses questions rather than explaining anything.

title: Argument that crypto fails basic currency tests
why: Opinion arguing crypto lacks insured deposits, price stability and recoverability; a position summary without deep technical explanation.

title: Typical COVID-19 symptom timeline and severity split
why: About 80% of cases are mild and 5% critical; severe cases often reach ARDS around day 8, with ICU admission most likely near day 10.
